honest_note: Rendered by the sld-sandbox cartridge since v9.143 (202609071005): a dashed line converter to converter and a node mid-line. Arrival wired in v9.146 (202609071232): a MAP link carrying interconnector=<BMRS> hands over from the project lane, the span is framed, and each converter is measured within its own search budget. This config declares the layer; the cartridge draws it.

reuse_offshore_rendering.why: An interconnector is shaped exactly like an offshore project as far as the Atlas is concerned: a name, a technology, a reference and a point. Reusing the offshore path means no new styling, no new card and no new MAP behaviour.
reuse_offshore_rendering.reference_value: the BMRS code, e.g. INTNED, standing in for a REPD ref
reuse_offshore_rendering.arrival_point: SUPERSEDED: not the midpoint; see arrival_model
reuse_offshore_rendering.consequence: SUPERSEDED: an interconnector has its own arrival branch; see arrival_model

geometry_contract.must_be_labelled: A straight line, never a cable route.
geometry_contract.what_it_measures: Separation between converter stations, not cable length.

BritNed.source: BritNed Development Ltd v ABB AB [2018] EWHC 2616 (Ch)
BritNed.reading: The straight line is within 4.3 per cent of the surveyed submarine cable on this link. That is one observation and not a constant: measure each link before applying a factor to it.

geometry_contract.future: Bend computation refines this same geometry; it does not replace it.

both_sides_compute.intent: Fire the existing grid engine from each converter station in turn, so a link reports what it connects to at both ends rather than only the GB end.
both_sides_compute.gb_end: Already in our own substation data for all ten links.
both_sides_compute.caution: The per-end search budget is the radius box value (the engine's onshore limit, 10 km at boot on the measured run; 40 km when the box is empty). A converter sits inside a substation compound, so the GB end scores ~0 km; a far end has no payload and is reported as absent coverage.

sources.flow_data: globalgrid2050 uk_energy_tracking_v6 — 70 rows, joined on bmrsCode (superseding the capacity-only reference csv)
sources.existing_ui: globalgrid2050 grid_engine/202609060305-interconnectors/index.html — the Interconnector Workbench, which names all ten links and currently carries no coordinates. This data is what it is missing.

coverage.why_the_rest_are_missing: OpenStreetMap holds 596 power=converter elements in the bbox but only 43 carry a name, and the unnamed ones cannot be matched to a link. The remaining eight need either a named OSM element or a TSO navigational publication, which is the stronger source because a TSO is obliged to tell mariners where its assets are.

electricity_data.join_key: bmrsCode — the same code this layer keys on, so geometry and flows land in one artefact
electricity_data.sign_convention: Imports are positive MWh. Exports are negative MWh. Carry this into any UI: a negative net is GB exporting, not missing data.
electricity_data.note: v5 is price history and grid frequency; the interconnector series begins at v6. Per-link import/export MWh files sit beside the index, one pair per link.

net_position_2020_2026_twh.reading: Every continental link is a net import to GB across the period; all three Ireland and Northern Ireland links are net exports from GB. Stated as a measurement over 2020-2026, not as a claim about any single year.

arrival_model.superseded: An earlier version of this file said the MAP button, the arrival and the grid engine would treat an interconnector exactly as a wind farm, arriving at the midpoint. That was wrong and was measured wrong: a BritNed midpoint is 59.2 km from the nearest substation and the far end resolves to Lowestoft at 165.9 km because the payload is GB only.
arrival_model.model: -distance-interconnectors-distance+: the span is unbounded; each converter is searched within the ordinary onshore budget, which the radius box overrides. 40km <- Grain --[ BritNed 234.9 km ]-- Maasvlakte -> 40km
arrival_model.anchor: the node drawn mid-line is a label anchor, not a location; measured, it is the planar mean of the converter coordinates, 1.44 km from the great-circle midpoint on BritNed
arrival_model.gb_end: measured against the arrival lane's published qualifying substations once the payload has arrived; Grain at 0 km with 20 within 10 km, Bicker Fen at 0.001 km with 8 within 10 km (offline, 2026-09-07)
arrival_model.far_end: no substation payload outside GB; reported as absent coverage, never as absence of connection
arrival_model.no_far_converter: no line is drawn; the map flies to the GB converter, measures it, and states the other end is not located
